title: Role Boundary Visualizer — wireframe brainstorm and grooming
body:
Purpose:
This is an exploratory wireframe + backlog grooming doc for a new console surface: the Role Boundary Visualizer (RBV). RBV aims to help org and team admins quickly understand the effective permissions each role gives across resources, identify privilege overlaps, and act (rotate keys, restrict role, create scoped service account) from a compact right-rail without leaving the page.

High-level goals:
- Make permission boundaries visible at-a-glance (no need to open multiple role pages).
- Surface risky combinations (role A + token X => broad access).
- Provide fast remediation actions inline (revoke token, create least-priv SA, start canary rollout).
- Integrate audit events related to the selected role/entity in a condensed timeline.

Audience:
- Org admins doing periodic access reviews
- Platform engineers onboarding service accounts
- SecOps investigating anomalies with quick contextual actions

Wireframe notes (sketch-level):
1) Primary canvas (left): resource map
   - Left column: actor list (users, groups, service accounts). Each actor row shows: avatar/initials, principal name, primary role badges, last-active timestamp.
   - Middle column: vertical swimlanes by resource type (Projects, Models, Deployments, Keys). Connectors show which actor has access to which resource. Hovering an edge highlights exact permissions.
   - Right column (compact details): when an actor is selected, show role cards with microcopy: role name, top 3 permissions, number of resources affected, & risk score (0-100).

2) Right-rail (persistent, sticky): Role Boundary Card + Audit Feed + Quick Actions
   - Top: Role Boundary Card (title: "Role: Deployment-Write")
     - Snapshot: scope (org/team/project), role type (predefined/custom), members count, risk score + brief rationale (e.g., "Can create and delete deployments across all projects").
     - Visual: mini Venn diagram showing overlap with other roles (hovering a slice filters the canvas).
   - Middle: Recent Audit events tied to role (compact list, show event type, actor, resource, time). Click expands modal with full audit row.
   - Bottom: Quick Actions (primary buttons): Revoke API keys (opens modal listing keys by age/last-used), Create Scoped Service Account (guided flow), Start Role Rollout (canary config modal), Add Constraint (policy condition wizard).

3) Token/Key lifecycle inset (inline modals)
   - When "Revoke API keys" clicked: modal shows keys table (id, created_at, last_used, scope, tag). Bulk select + revoke + optional replacement SA creation suggestion. Suggestion logic: if key last_used by deployment X, offer to create SA scoped to "deployment-X" with same minimal perms.

Microcopy snippets (for UX):
- Risk score tooltip: "Calculated from permission breadth, cross-role overlap, and last-used exposure. Not a verdict — use as a guide."
- Quick action: "Create scoped service account — recommended when a long-lived key is in use by a single deployment."
- Audit entry: "API Key used by deployment 'ingest-collector' to call model inference on prod-model-v3."

Backlog grooming (rough priorities, estimates):
- RBV: initial canvas + actor/resource graph (MVP) — priority P0, 3 sprints (Frontend 6w, Backend 4w)
- Right-rail: Role Boundary Card + risk score + quick actions (MVP) — P0, 2 sprints (Frontend 4w, API 2w)
- Audit feed integration (condensed events, filter by role) — P1, 1 sprint (API work to tie events)
- Token lifecycle modal w/ replacement SA suggestion alpha — P1, 1 sprint + security review
- Role overlap heatmap (UI perf heavy) — P2, 2 sprints, research on graph perf
- E2E acceptance tests + canary rollout telemetry — P0, 1 sprint (SRE + QA)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Risk score algorithm: what signals do we include? (permission breadth, resource criticality, cross-role multiplicity, last use recency). Who signs off? (research + security).
- Data volume: resource graph could be huge for orgs with many projects. Should we sample/limit to first N resources and provide filters? (UX/Engineering tradeoff).
- RBAC read model: do we reuse existing policy API or build a read-optimized materialized view? If the latter, runbook for refresh cadence.
- Quick action guardrails: what approvals are required to auto-create SAs or revoke keys? Should we require two-step approval for high-risk roles?

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- User can filter by actor or role and see immediate visual highlights on the canvas.
- Right-rail shows at least 5 recent audit events for the selected role/principal.
- From the right-rail, user can launch Revoke API keys modal and perform a revoke action in sandbox (simulated), and optionally trigger SA creation flow.
- Risk score visible and explained via tooltip.

Privacy & Security notes:
- Audit feed must respect retention and masking policies. Do not show raw tokens.
- SA creation flow must integrate with KMS key rotation policy and org limits.

Design constraints / performance:
- Initial canvas should cap nodes at 200 for interactivity; provide a server-side filter to show "top 200 by activity".
- All right-rail actions should be async with operation IDs surfaced and linkable to Console Activity log.

Proposed next steps (short-term):
1) Sync with Security (Diego) on risk score signals and approval guardrails (this week).
2) Engineering feasibility spike: prototype actor->resource read model and small graph API (2wk spike).
3) Design: produce two medium-fidelity wireframes (compact + expanded) for usability testing (1wk).
4) Product: create JIRA epic + initial tickets, align on P0 scope for next sprint.

Notes from brainstorming session (raw bullets):
- Could we reuse the "compact quick actions" pattern from docs console? Keep button sizes small, favor dropdown for secondary ops.
- Idea: when role overlap slice is tiny (<5% overlap), suggest automatic consolidation into a single role template.
- Consider a "what-if" sandbox toggler: simulate removing a role and show potentially impacted resources. Useful for change management.
- For very large orgs, allow CSV export of actor->resource mapping for offline analysis.

References and inspiration:
- Gated access explorer (internal research deck, link in linked_artifacts)
__notes: This doc is intentionally informal and sketch-focused — majority of content is raw brainstorming for internal review.
